3.name: third person
3.plain: anyone or anything else: he, she, it, they

M.name: masculine
M.plain: one of the two genders; also used for mixed groups

DEF.name: definite article
DEF.plain: the prefix ha- 'the', which doubles the next consonant

QTL.name: qatal (suffix conjugation)
QTL.plain: the verb form that marks person with endings, mostly used for completed events: he did, he has done

Q.name: question particle
Q.plain: the prefix hă- that turns a statement into a yes/no question

OBJ.name: object marker
OBJ.plain: the word ʾēt (ʾet-, ʾōt-) placed before a definite direct object; it has no English equivalent

DU.name: dual
DU.plain: exactly two, or a natural pair such as hands or eyes

CSTR.name: construct state
CSTR.plain: the bound form a noun takes when another noun or a suffix follows it: 'word of'

YQTL.name: yiqtol (long prefix conjugation)
YQTL.plain: the verb form that marks person with prefixes, used mostly for future, habitual and modal events: he will do, he used to do, he may do

WAYY.name: wayyiqtol prefix
WAYY.plain: the prefix wa- plus doubling that turns a short prefix form into the main past-narrative verb: and he did

WQTL.name: weqatal prefix
WQTL.plain: the prefix wə- on a qatal form when it continues a command, future or habit: and he will do

JUSS.name: jussive
JUSS.plain: the short prefix form used to wish or command for a third person, and with ʾal for 'do not': let him do

COH.name: cohortative
COH.plain: the first-person prefix form lengthened with -â, expressing resolve or request: let me do, let us do

PTCP.name: participle
PTCP.plain: a verbal adjective that can also act as a noun or as 'is doing'

PASS.name: passive
PASS.plain: the subject undergoes the action; used here of the qal passive participle (šāmûr 'guarded')

INF.name: infinitive construct
INF.plain: the verbal noun used after prepositions: to do, when doing

NIPH.name: niphal
NIPH.plain: the n-stem, mostly passive or middle: was guarded, guarded himself

PIEL.name: piel
PIEL.plain: the stem that doubles the middle root letter, often making a state happen or intensifying

HIPH.name: hiphil
HIPH.plain: the h-stem, mostly causative: made someone do

HOPH.name: hophal
HOPH.plain: the passive of the hiphil: was made to do

HITP.name: hithpael
HITP.plain: the stem with the prefix hit-, mostly reflexive or reciprocal: did to or for oneself, to each other

DIR.name: directional ending
DIR.plain: the unstressed ending -â meaning 'towards': to Egypt, homewards

REL.name: relative marker
REL.plain: the word ʾăšer (later še-) that opens a clause describing a noun: who, which, that

INFABS.name: infinitive absolute
INFABS.plain: the free verbal noun used for emphasis, for an accompanying action, or as a command

terms.root: The two or three consonants that carry a word's core meaning (hbo-00-02, hbo-01-01).
terms.pattern: The arrangement of vowels and extra letters around a root that makes a particular kind of word (hbo-00-02).
terms.final form: The shape five letters take at the end of a word (hbo-01-01).
terms.Palaeo-Hebrew: The older Hebrew alphabet used before the square script (hbo-01-01).
terms.square script: The Aramaic-derived letter forms in which the Bible has come down (hbo-01-01).
terms.guttural: One of the throat letters alef, he, ḥet, ʿayin, and often resh (hbo-01-02).
terms.emphatic: One of the consonants ṭet, ṣade, qof, probably pronounced with extra constriction (hbo-01-02).
terms.vowel points: The dots and dashes added to the consonants to show vowels (hbo-01-03).
terms.vowel letter: A consonant letter used to show a vowel (mater lectionis) (hbo-01-04).
terms.full spelling: Spelling with a vowel letter; defective spelling leaves it out (hbo-01-04).
terms.shewa: The two-dot mark under a letter: vocal (a short murmured vowel) or silent (no vowel) (hbo-01-05).
terms.hatef vowel: A shewa combined with a vowel sign, used under gutturals (hbo-01-05).
terms.open syllable: A syllable ending in a vowel (hbo-01-06).
terms.closed syllable: A syllable ending in a consonant (hbo-01-06).
terms.qameṣ ḥaṭuf: The qameṣ sign read as short o in a closed unstressed syllable (hbo-01-06).
terms.furtive pataḥ: A short a slipped in before a final guttural (hbo-01-06).
terms.meteg: A small vertical stroke marking secondary stress (hbo-01-06).
terms.dagesh lene: A dot showing a hard (stop) pronunciation of a begadkefat letter (hbo-01-07).
terms.begadkefat: The six letters b g d k p t, each with a hard and a soft pronunciation (hbo-01-07).
terms.mappiq: A dot in final he showing it is a real consonant (hbo-01-07).
terms.segolate: A noun of the meleḵ type, stressed on the first syllable with a helping vowel (hbo-01-08).
terms.maqqef: A hyphen joining words into one stress unit (hbo-01-08).
terms.pause: The form a word takes at a major break in the verse (hbo-01-08).
terms.accents: The cantillation marks, which also mark stress and punctuation (hbo-01-09).
terms.disjunctive accent: An accent that marks a break (hbo-01-09).
terms.conjunctive accent: An accent that joins a word to the next (hbo-01-09).
terms.ketiv: What is written in the consonantal text (hbo-01-09).
terms.qere: What is read aloud where it differs from the ketiv (hbo-01-09).
terms.perpetual qere: A word always read differently from its spelling, such as the divine name (hbo-01-09).
terms.transliteration: Writing Hebrew letter for letter in Latin letters (hbo-01-10).
